title: Compact density: toolbar collapse, table row wrap, chart legend overflow - cross-browser QA & triage
creator: Claire Duarte
description: Summary: Run focused cross-browser QA for the 'compact density' surface updates touching toolbar collapse behavior, table row wrapping, and chart legend overflow. Primary goals: identify reproducible regressions on Safari (iOS/macOS) and Firefox (desktop/Android), capture device-specific layout shifts, validate token scaling (spacing/typography) in compact mode, and triage defects into fixable engineering/design tasks. Background: compact density tokens were introduced to support higher information density in the Console; early dogfood surfaced inconsistent collapse thresholds for the left toolbar and chart legend clipping when the container width hits 320-420px. Several reports also show table rows wrapping and pushing pagination controls off-screen on iOS Safari with momentum scroll enabled.
reproducibility_steps: 1) Open Console > Projects list on iPhone 12 (iOS 16.4) Safari; set zoom 100% and toggle Compact Density in user prefs
2) Resize window to 360x800 on Android Pixel 5 Firefox, reproduce table with long cell content (user agent: test dataset 'long-names.csv')
3) Trigger toolbar collapse by narrowing viewport to 320px then expand; observe element overlap and hit-target regressions
4) Load dashboard with chart that has 5 legends and compact tokens; reduce width to 420px and inspect clipping/overflow and legend wrap behavior
5) Run with reduced-motion enabled and with CSS GPU compositing disabled to surface animation-induced layout shifts
observed_issues: A) Left toolbar collapse uses transform-based animation that causes stacking context change; on iOS Safari the collapsed toolbar overlaps toast notifications (severity: P1)
B) Table row wrapping: long inline tokens cause entire row height increase and push pagination off-canvas on mobile (severity: P1)
C) Chart legend overflow: legend items are clipped rather than wrapping/scrolling under compact mode at 360-420px (severity: P2)
D) Button hit target dip: density tokens reduced padding below 32px touch recommendation on Android Firefox leading to missed taps (severity: P2)
E) Typography token mismatch: compact font scale uses 12px but line-height collapses on Safari, causing truncation in multi-line cells (severity: P2)
F) Momentum scroll + sticky headers: sticky table header jumps on iOS Safari when table row wraps (severity: P1)
G) RTL edge cases: toolbar collapse ordering flips but icon clipping remains (severity: P3)
H) Accessibility: compact-mode focus ring is 1px and low contrast on dark tokens (severity: P2)
I) Intermittent reflow when switching between density modes on slower devices (severity: P2)
triage_decisions: 1) Immediate engineering fixes (hotpath): toolbar overlap (A), pagination off-canvas (B), sticky header jump (F) — assign ENG tickets and block release until P1 fixes available
2) Medium priority (sprint): button hit target (D), typography token mismatch (E), legend overflow (C) — implement CSS min-width/min-height tokens and flexible legend flow
3) Low priority/PD: RTL polish (G), focus contrast tweaks (H) and perf reflow mitigation (I) — schedule in next design pass
4) Accessibility: create a focused a11y test case for compact mode and add to the regression suite (owner: UX Accessibility)
5) For toolbar animation, prefer opacity + translateY with will-change over scale transforms to avoid stacking context jumps on mobile WebKit

decisions: Use a compact-token scale table that preserves a 32px minimum touchable area for interactive controls. This means tokens can visually shrink but containers maintain the min target.
Avoid transform: scale for toolbar collapse; use translateX/translateY + opacity to prevent stacking context issues on WebKit.
Implement responsive legend flow: prefer multi-line wrapping with a max-height + scroll for extremely narrow widths rather than clipping.
Add focused regression tests: iOS Safari (latest), Firefox Android latest, desktop Firefox macOS; include reduced-motion and RTL permutations.
